title: Introduce batch-governor constraint solver and quant fallback
author: Maya Singh
description: Context: tenants with mixed latency/cost targets need an automated, policy-driven way to choose batching shapes and a safe quantization fallback when capacity or price pressure requires it. This PR introduces a 'Batch Governor' constraint solver that synthesizes per-tenant runtime batch policies from SLOs and budget envelopes, plus an automated compact-quant fallback selector that can be rolled out gently per-tenant. Motivation: prior heuristics encoded in the batch router were brittle and required manual tuning; teams spent time crafting tenant-specific defaults. The solver encodes soft constraints (latency p95/p99, cost-per-token target, GPU slot utilization) and outputs prioritized candidate batch shapes and an ordered set of quantization profiles (e.g., compact-8, compact-4, std-16). Key changes in this PR: - New package pkg/batch/governor: constraint solver and policy compiler (LP-guided greedy annealer for large tenant spaces). - Quant fallback profiles added in config/quant-profiles.yaml and a small runtime adaptor that validates quality regression thresholds before applying. - Gentle tenant rollout: the tenant defaults propagator supports a "gentleRoll" phase that ramps policy changes across traffic slices and can auto-revert on quality or latency regressions. - Telemetry: new prefilling and decision metrics (telemetry/prefill/metrics.yaml) and token-level cost attribution tags (batch_governor.variant, quant_applied) for downstream billing and SLO dashboards. - CLI tool cli/prefill-sim that lets SRE/product test constraints against replayed traffic and produces a reconciliation diff. - E2E test harness and unit tests for solver stability/tested worst-case with synthetic microbursts. Design notes: the solver is intentionally conservative: it prefers solutions that maintain p99 latency within configured SLO slack and treats quantization changes as last-resort, only recommended when cost projections exceed tenant budget for 3 consecutive windows. The quant adapter requires a small, signed quality token (from offline eval) before an aggressive quant profile is allowed automatically. Rollout plan and risk mitigations: - Stage 1: default off; enable for selected beta tenants and run CLI dry runs (prefill-sim) for 48h. - Stage 2: enable gentleRoll with 1%->10%->50%->100% traffic steps, monitor batch_governor.variant and quant_applied metrics. - Automated safety hooks: if repro-weighted ROUGE/QA delta > configured threshold OR p99 increases beyond slack, the propagator auto-reverts and opens an incident. Benchmarks (internal): - Simulated retail chat workload: expected unit-cost reduction ~12-16% at steady-state with no measurable p99 regression (within 5% slack); cold-start microburst tail improved by ~8% from smarter shapes. - Large multi-turn assistant traces: when forced to apply compact-8 fallback, we observed 2.3% quality delta on our eval set; the signed quality token requirement prevents blind rollouts. Checklist: - [x] Constraint solver implementation and unit tests - [x] Quant profile definitions and adapter - [x] Prefill simulation CLI and e2e tests - [x] Telemetry metrics and dashboard wiring - [x] Docs: docs/tenant-rollout.md and runtime README - [x] Add gradual rollout/gentleRoll wiring at propagator surface How to review: focus on solver heuristics (pkg/batch/governor/solver.go), quant safety checks (pkg/quant/adapter.go), and the prefilling telemetry tags. The CLI is low-risk and useful for reproducing results (cli/prefill-sim). Related work: ENG-1248 (policy-as-code for batching), ENG-1310 (quant fallback contract), SUP-4421 (support request for tenant X high-cost anomalies). RFC: internal link to RFC: https://linear.app/redwood/rfcs/batch-governor (see linked Linear tickets).

release_notes: - Add Batch Governor: a constraint solver that synthesizes tenant batching policies from SLOs and budget envelopes; supports soft constraints and prioritization.; - Introduce compact quant fallback profiles and safety-adapter that requires signed offline-quality tokens before autopromote.; - CLI tool (prefill-sim) to simulate constraints against historical traffic and produce reconciliation diffs.; - Telemetry tags for batch_governor.variant and quant_applied, plus dashboard wiring for rollout monitoring.
qa_and_rollout: Beta rollout to selected tenants, CLI dry runs for 48h, gentleRoll traffic ramp (1->10->50->100%), automatic revert on quality or latency regression. Ops runbook added to docs/tenant-rollout.md.
post_merge_actions: 1) Backfill signed quality tokens for currently enrolled tenants; 2) Enable PREFILL_GOVERNOR for beta tenants; 3) Create dashboards for batch_governor.variant/quant_applied; 4) Schedule 72h post-rollout evaluation.
notes_for_eng: This PR focuses on synthesis and policy generation; runtime enforcement is lightweight but depends on existing dispatcher hooks. If you plan to extend the solver, prefer adding soft-constraint weights in compiler.go rather than in dispatcher to keep runtime deterministic.
